text:
alex: ran a 30min perf sweep on ingress-host yesterday. surprising host-side cost: ~35% CPU in parsing/tokenization + syscalls when seq_len > 512. attached flame showed kernel-selection spikes around model candidates.

maria: wow, 35% is large. was this before or after the kernel-selector change last week? commit 0a3f2b9

alex: after. i bisected — when selector does fallback to int8 kernel on some batches we see extra memcpy and K/V miss churn. repro below.

jun: can you paste the hot stack? also which distro/kernel? sometimes splice/sendfile helps for streaming chunks.

alex: linux 6.3 on our dedicated hosts. perf top (summarized):

```
34.2%  parse_request
18.9%  kernel_selector::choose
12.3%  __memcpy_fromiovec
8.1%   http2_frame_recv
6.5%   kv_cache_lookup
```

alex: most of the memcpy comes from converting framed chunks into a single buffer for tokenization. we copy -> tokenize -> push into runtime; when kv cache misses we do another copy for k/v serialization.

sara: do we have a streaming parser that avoids full-merge? iirc we used a framed-reader that coalesces to simplify tokenizer, but that is the copy source.

maria: yes we intentionally coalesced to simplify tokenizer because splitter had bugs. maybe revert to zero-copy streaming and make tokenizer tolerant of fragmented input.

jun: alternative: move tokenization into the ingress worker pool thread that owns the socket buffer so we can tokenize in-place and avoid the intermediate copy. overhead tradeoffs: more CPU on ingress, but fewer memcopies and lower tail latency.

tim: worth canarying. propose: create variant ingress-host-parse-lite that does in-place tokenization + non-blocking KV async lookup. route 5% traffic.

alex: also saw HTTP/2 window stalls causing small writes to hammer epoll. coalescing outbound frames reduced syscalls 3x in a quick patch.

maria: can you share the patch? small helper that batches outbound frames into a single write?

alex: yep. snippet used in prototype:

```
// coalesce frames up to 64KB or 8 frames
void flush_outbound(Socket s, vector<Frame>& q) {
  Buffer b;
  while (!q.empty() && b.size() < 65536 && frames < 8) b.append(q.pop_front());
  send(s, b.ptr(), b.len(), 0);
}
```

alex: result: syscall rate down 2.9x, p95 latency for 1-token requests down ~18%.

jun: for KV cache behavior: if lookup is on hot path and misses cause sync fallback to remote store, that kills throughput. we should use prefetching and a lightweight bloom check before full lookup.

sara: +1. we can add a small in-memory bloom per worker (4KB) to avoid most cold misses. false positives OK. reduces RPCs.

maria: i measured RPC cost: avg 2.1ms for a KV miss (internal), miss rate ~0.6% at 99th percentile workloads spikes -> that becomes a big tail.

tim: rollout plan suggestion:
- create feature flag ingress_parse_inplace
- add bloom pre-check for kv (kv_bloom=true)
- route 5% traffic to canary variant with both enabled
- collect tokenization CPU, memcpy counts, syscall rate, p95/p99 lat

jun: one more: kernel-selector should expose a "copy-cost" estimate. when evaluating kernel choices, include estimated host-copy overhead to prefer kernels that minimize cross-boundary copies for short sequences.

alex: agreed. currently selector only weights GPU completion time and memory footprint. adding host-cost term moved perf for <=128 tokens by ~12% in my simulation.

maria: i can update selector config schema. small example config change:

```
{
  "selector": {
    "weights": {
      "gpu_time": 0.7,
      "mem": 0.2,
      "host_copy_cost": 0.1
    }
  }
}
```

sara: careful with overfitting to lab benchmarks. add an online-learning weight tuner that slowly updates weights based on real metrics.

tim: opsbot can you start canary rollout when we merge the branch? will monitor.

opsbot: deploybot: canary job started for branch "ingress-parse-inplace" -> 5% hosts. build 2026.03.18.10. log: https://ci.internal/2026/ingress-parse-inplace :rocket:

jun: one more micro: avoid Json.parse for the control envelope. use a tiny custom header parser (80% smaller parse cost). we did this in edge-proxy before.

alex: benchmark: JSON parse for envelope ~120us, custom fastproto ~18us. big win for many tiny requests.

maria: ok i'll draft a PR that wires up:
- ingress_parse_inplace feature flag
- kv_bloom per worker
- selector host_copy_cost weight
- fastproto envelope parsing

tim: lets collect metrics for 48h on canary, then 25% ramp if no regressions. :eyes:

sara: tagging @jun for selector changes and @alex for ingress patches.

jun: on it. will also add a small perf test that simulates seq_len distribution and measures memcpy counts.

alex: thanks team. will put the perf artifacts in the perf-uploads folder and leave a short runbook for rollback (disable flag). :thumbsup:
